item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hm. It doesn't do much for me. It reminds me a bit of the MAN EGGS, which I remember not finding particularly good either. It just doesn't go very far beyond its core concept which is a bit much to take seriously in my opinion (a tree whose fruits are hanged men? No… just no), so it's a neutral vote for me as I feel a rewrite could make it a very good SCP.

There are also a couple things that bother me. For starters, feeding the contained carnivores instances of SCP-936-2 seems awfully irresponsible of the SCP Foundation. They have no idea what it'll do to these animals, especially since grafting experiments showed unexpected results, it's fair to consider that it might have similar effects on a nimals who eat them.

Then, there's the way it was recovered as it is stated that it was noticed after people reported an unusually high amount of suicides. Fair enough, but nobody found it weird that they were hanging not from ropes but from stems coming from the trees? And that they were surrounded with weird vegetal shells? Not even SCP Foundation agents who first went with a cognitohazard theory?

Finally, there are two expungements I find weird:

SCP-936 is capable of forming clonal colonies, the ol[DATA EXPUNGED].

Note: This might explain why [DATA EXPUNGED]gmen - Researcher Eisenberg

For what reason are words cut off by the "[DATA EXPUNGED]" tag? And yeah, I know you're not the only one doing that and it confuses me every time it shows up. Seriously, what's the logic behind that?

Downvoted for these reasons. I might switch to neutral if these things are fixed, or if I just look back at this and feel like I might've been too harsh.

item.title: Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
This article is up for review, please check it out! It needs more attention.

I actually liked most of this. A so-so idea executed decently. However, I didn't really care for the recovery log or the addenda. I dunno if the description of how the plants work is scientifically accurate(at least to the degree that something like this can stick to science) and will leave that to our resident botanists to decide. I didn't like the recovery log because it seemed kind of a stupid way for it to be found. Suicide rates going up? C'mon, there's gotta be something better than that here. The test logs didn't add much to the idea, I think, and could be cut without changing much. The last addenda…. actually, the last one is fine. I think it deserves to stick around. Overall, despite my misgivings for some of this, I found it cool enough to warrant an upvote from me.

item.title: What I was reminded of...
item.content:encoded:
Southern trees bear a strange fruit,
Blood on the leaves and blood at the root,
Black bodies swinging in the southern breeze,
Strange fruit hanging from the poplar trees.

Pastoral scene of the gallant south,
The bulging eyes and the twisted mouth,
Scent of magnolias, sweet and fresh,
Then the sudden smell of burning flesh.

Here is fruit for the crows to pluck,
For the rain to gather, for the wind to suck,
For the sun to rot, for the trees to drop,
Here is a strange and bitter crop.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The appearance specifically as hanged humans adds that bit of biological implausibility which makes this a bit scary. I could see a plant possibly evolving something that seems like dead meat so as to spread the seed pods, but it would seem like something smaller, like a kitten tree, would be more likely to attract scavengers. That said, it's also possible that the tree is specifically geared toward the fruit being relocated to the well-fertilized area of the graveyard… and that adaptation to human foibles makes it all the scarier.

Up-voted.
